chunks: The exalted Sheikh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Asbat narrated to us. He said: I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrating from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), that the Messenger of Allah (may God bless him and his family) said:
None of the proverbs of the prophets remain except the saying of the people: If you feel no shame, then do what you wish.

key_terms.أمثال الأنبياء: Amthal al-Anbiya' - proverbs of the prophets, collective prophetic wisdom
key_terms.حياء: Haya' - shame, modesty, the inner moral sense that restrains wrongdoing

ai.seo_question: What is the famous prophetic proverb 'If you feel no shame, then do what you wish'?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves a celebrated prophetic proverb transmitted through Imam al-Rida (AS) back to the Prophet (S). The saying 'If you feel no shame, then do what you wish' is identified as the sole surviving proverb from the collective wisdom of all prophets. Its meaning is not a permission to do whatever one wishes, but rather a rebuke: shame (haya') is the internal moral compass that restrains wrongdoing. Without it, a person will inevitably do whatever they please without moral constraint. The original audience understood this as elevating haya' to the rank of the most essential prophetic teaching across all dispensations.
